posts.title: Xiaomi unveils 3-nm Xring D100 smart-driving chip, plans commercial use in 2027
posts.summary:
Xiaomi said the Xring D100 is China's first high-computing-power smart-driving chip built on a 3-nm process and can run models with up to 200 billion parameters locally.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xiaomi has unveiled the Xring D100, China's first 3-nm smart-driving chip, capable of running large language models with up to 200 billion parameters locally.
The chip has completed validation and is slated for commercial deployment in 2027, signaling a strategic shift toward vertical integration of automotive hardware.
Xiaomi has invested over 21 billion yuan in its semiconductor division, which now employs nearly 3,000 experts to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia.
The move intensifies competition among Chinese EV makers, such as Nio and Li Auto, who are increasingly developing proprietary silicon to optimize AI performance and costs.

posts.title: Xpeng to launch G9L in September, Mona L05 in Q4 as it targets 60,000 monthly sales
posts.summary:
Xpeng has begun double-shift production of the Mona L03 SUV and is working with suppliers to accelerate the capacity ramp-up.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Xpeng aims to reach 60,000 monthly vehicle deliveries in Q4 2026, representing a 58% increase over July's performance.
The company is launching the G9L flagship SUV in September and the Mona L05 in Q4 to expand its coverage across major SUV segments.
Production of the Mona L03 has shifted to a double-shift schedule to address supply-chain bottlenecks and meet growing demand.
The G9L features an 800-volt charging platform and offers both BEV and EREV variants, directly targeting competitors like Li Auto and Aito.

posts.title: Leapmotor stays profitable in H1 as margin and cash flow weaken
posts.summary:
Leapmotor's first-half net profit rose to 210 million yuan ($30.95 million), marking its third consecutive half-year of profitability.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Leapmotor reported a 210 million yuan net profit for H1 2026, marking its third consecutive half-year of profitability despite a 18.2% decline in non-IFRS adjusted net profit.
Gross margin narrowed to 11.7% from 14.1% year-on-year, driven by rising raw material costs and shifts in the vehicle product mix.
Free cash flow dropped 83.7% to 140 million yuan, largely due to increased procurement spending for inventory stocking.
Overseas expansion is accelerating, with exports reaching 96,294 vehicles in H1, already surpassing the total export volume for the full year 2025.

posts.title: Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below
posts.summary:
Chips are getting bigger, more modular, and much more capable as new innovations mix with existing processes and long-researched projects go mainstream.
The post Multi-Die Assemblies Dominate At 2nm And Below appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The semiconductor industry is shifting toward multi-die assemblies and heterogeneous integration as traditional monolithic scaling fails to meet the performance requirements of modern AI workloads.
Performance gains are no longer driven solely by transistor shrinking, as the demand for compute power has outpaced the physical limits of reticle-sized dies.
The rise of agentic AI necessitates complex architectures that combine CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators, requiring AI-driven design tools to manage manufacturability and validation.

Achieving the industry goal of two orders of magnitude improvement in performance-per-watt will require a fundamental realignment of manufacturing processes, prioritizing advanced packaging and chiplet-based designs.

posts.title: The Download: kids outlearning AI, and space travel agents
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why Teaching a computer to use human language requires an inhuman amount of data. An LLM can easily churn through a hundred thousand times…
bullets: A growing bipartisan political backlash against AI data centers is emerging in the US, with concerns centering on their massive energy consumption and environmental impact.
The commercial space sector is evolving into a luxury service market, with firms like SpaceVIP positioning themselves as 'space travel agents' for private missions to the ISS.
Researchers are investigating the 'data efficiency gap' between human children and LLMs, as current AI models require orders of magnitude more data to achieve linguistic fluency than a human child.
